market.question: US-Iran Hormuz Agreement by October 15?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if a diplomatic agreement between the United States and Iran over traffic in the strait of Hormuz is announced by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET.

A diplomatic agreement refers to an official agreement, treaty, deal, or substantially similar diplomatic instrument that establishes agreed actions, policies, obligations, or commitments between the United States and Iran.

A qualifying diplomatic agreement must establish Iranian policies, obligations, or commitments  aimed at permitting, restoring, or increasing vessel or shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.

All listed countries must announce their acceptance of the same qualifying diplomatic agreement for the Payout Condition to be met. A joint announcement will qualify, as will separate announcements from each entity of its own acceptance of an agreement which, taken together, directly indicate that all the listed countries accepted the same agreement. Separate announcements of individual policies will not qualify if the policies are not announced as part of a diplomatic agreement.

Each announcement must be a declarative statement that clearly and unambiguously communicates acceptance of an agreement. Statements that reference ongoing negotiations or a prospective agreement, or that allude to or express support for an agreement without confirming acceptance of the agreement, do not qualify. A qualifying announcement need not reference the agreement by name or use specific terminology, provided it clearly communicates acceptance of an agreement.
 
Whether announcements from the listed countries represent a diplomatic agreement and whether such an agreement qualifies will be primarily determined through the announcements themselves. Where an announcement is made by all listed countries but, based on the announcements, it remains ambiguous whether the announcements represent a qualifying diplomatic agreement between the countries, this market will remain open until either i) definitive confirmation that the announcements represent a qualifying diplomatic agreement between the listed entities is achieved through further announcements from the listed countries or a consensus of credible reporting or ii) 14 calendar days (ET) have passed after the date that the last country made their first potentially qualifying announcement. If, at the end of the fourteenth calendar day, no definitive confirmation has been achieved, this market will resolve based on the totality of information available from the resolution sources at that time. No single statement, denial, or presentation of evidence will govern where it is contradicted by the totality of information.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from the governments of the United States and Iran and a consensus of credible reporting.

To count for resolution, the individual must be elected by the National Assembly and be formally sworn-in, resulting in the official formation of a new government. Any interim or caretaker Prime Minister who is not elected by the National Assembly will not count toward the resolution of this market.

If no such Prime Minister takes office by June 30, 2028, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “Other”.

This market will resolve based on a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve solely based on official information from the Serbian government.

recent_facts.fact: On September 9, 2026, President Vučić dissolved the National Assembly and called a snap parliamentary election for October 25, 2026. That is the same day this question closes. A new government needs a vote in the newly elected Assembly afterwards, so a PM cannot be sworn in by the close date.

Vučić resigned as president on September 27, 2026, to run for prime minister. The constitution bars him from a third presidential term. Ana Brnabić, the outgoing Assembly speaker, became acting president, and a presidential election must be held within 90 days of the resignation.

The Republic Electoral Commission (RIK) approved the list 'Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia' with 209,130 valid signatures. Vučić is first on the list and is the SNS coalition's named candidate for prime minister.

On October 3, 2026, Vučić opened his campaign for prime minister at Belgrade's largest indoor arena. If SNS wins a majority, the new parliament would elect him PM. His main rival is the student-led Student List.

The National Assembly has 250 seats and 126 are needed for a majority. Seats are filled by closed-list proportional representation from one nationwide constituency, using D'Hondt with a 3% threshold (waived for minority parties). At least 16 lists qualified, including Ivica Dačić's SPS-led 'Factor of Stability', NADA and European Serbia.
The current Prime Minister is Đuro Macut, an independent, in office since April 2025. He replaced Miloš Vučević, who resigned in January 2025 during the protests.

NSPM poll published September 30, 2026 (fieldwork early September): Student List 44.4%, SNS-led list 41.7%. Earlier polls showing the Student List ahead were NSPM on July 30 (39.6% vs 37.5%) and CRTA on July 15 (44.9% vs 35.7%).
The student movement registered 'Student List – Students Are Winning' with RIK. The first name on the list is doctor Ilija Srđanović.

UNVERIFIED: time from Serbian elections to a new government being sworn in: 2014, about 6 weeks (Mar 16 to Apr 27); 2016, about 3.5 months (Apr 24 to Aug 11); 2020, about 4 months (Jun 21 to Oct 28); 2022, about 7 months (Apr 3 to Oct 26); 2023, about 4.5 months (Dec 17, 2023 to May 2, 2024).

UNVERIFIED: Vučić led the SNS list and then became PM after the 2014 and 2016 elections, 2 of 2 cases. In 2020, 2022 and 2023 lists carried his name while he was president, but someone else became PM.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

In the case that the Resolution Source publishes data, sufficient to settle a Market, that is clearly erroneous and the result of technical or operational error, or of unauthorized interference with the Resolution Source or its data, the Market may remain open for a period of up to seven (7) calendar days (ET) from the time of the original release, in anticipation of a correction by the Resolution Source. If the Resolution Source publishes a corrected value within that period, that value will be eligible for resolution. If no corrected value is published within that period, Polymarket will issue a Clarification to determine whether the originally published value may be eligible for resolution, or whether other action is required to preserve the orderly functioning of the Market.

market.question: Will OpenAI not announce that it has resumed training by October 20, 2026?
market.rules:
On September 25, 2026, amid reports that its AI agents had probed U.S. government websites, including those of the Census Bureau and Education Department, OpenAI disclosed a pause in training, evaluation, and inference involving tool use for its most capable models.

This market will resolve according to the calendar date (ET) on which OpenAI announces that it has resumed training covered by the pause announced on September 25, 2026. If no qualifying announcement is made by 11:59 PM ET on October 20, 2026, this market will resolve to "Not resumed by October 20".

Resuming training means resuming, in part or in full, training suspended under the pause announced on September 25, 2026, including beginning a fresh training run in place of a suspended run.

A qualifying announcement must be made through OpenAI's official channels or by an authorized representative acting in an official capacity. The totality of the announcement and its surrounding context must clearly establish that training covered by the pause announced on September 25 has resumed, even if the announcement does not name the incident or specify the date the pause was announced.

Statements that training is permitted, planned, or expected to restart do not by themselves qualify. Training that was not subject to the pause announced on September 25, 2026, does not qualify.

This market will resolve to the date of the first qualifying announcement, regardless of whether the announcement is later modified or withdrawn, or training is subsequently paused again.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from OpenAI; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

recent_facts.fact: Guatemala hosts Suriname on Monday, October 5, 2026 at 6:00 PM Guatemala time (00:00 UTC Oct 6) at Estadio Manuel Felipe Carrera ('El Trébol') in Guatemala City. It is Matchday 4, the last group match, in League A Group B of the Concacaf Nations League.

Group B table before Matchday 4: Suriname 7 pts (2W 1D 0L, GF 5 GA 3), Jamaica 6, Guatemala 4 (1W 1D 1L, GF 8 GA 3, GD +5), then Honduras, Martinique and El Salvador on 3 each. The top two reach the quarter-finals. Teams play four group games each in a Swiss-style format.
Prensa Libre writes that Suriname clinches qualification with a win or a draw, and that Guatemala needs a win to keep its hopes alive. A win would put Guatemala on 7 points.

The first meeting, on October 2, 2026 in Paramaribo, finished Suriname 0-0 Guatemala. Suriname had most of the ball and the chances, and Guatemala goalkeeper Kenderson Navarro made 8 saves (Sofascore rating 8.2).

Guatemala striker Darwin Lom (The Strongest) is available again after serving a one-match suspension for yellow-card accumulation. Winger Óscar Santis is still ruled out with the muscle injury he picked up in the 6-0 win over El Salvador.

For the October 2 match, Guatemala was without Santis (injured), Rubio Rubín (injured) and Lom (suspended). Coach Luis Fernando Tena called up José Bolaños (Deportivo Mixco) and Jesús López (Xelajú) as emergency replacements. No dated update on Rubín's status was found.

Suriname's 24-man squad has 23 players at clubs abroad, including Gyrano Kerk (Erzurumspor), Kenneth Paal (Antalyaspor), Shaquille Pinas (Al-Kholood) and goalkeeper Etienne Vaessen (Groningen). No specific Suriname injury or suspension news for the return match was found.

The last time these teams met in Guatemala City was a World Cup qualifier on November 18, 2025, which Guatemala won 3-1 with goals from Lom, Olger Escobar and Santis. Guatemala had already been eliminated; Suriname went to the play-off.

Other recent meeting: Suriname 1-1 Guatemala in Paramaribo in a World Cup qualifier on October 10, 2025. That makes the last 3 meetings 1 Guatemala win and 2 draws (one win at home, two draws away). Three games is a very small sample.

Guatemala's group results so far: lost 2-3 away at Jamaica (Sep 25), beat El Salvador 6-0 (Sep 28) and drew 0-0 away at Suriname (Oct 2). Suriname's: won 3-2 at Honduras, beat Martinique 2-1, drew 0-0 with Guatemala.

The Active Month is the nearest listed contract, except during that contract's final three trading sessions. At the open of the third-to-last trading session, the next listed contract becomes the Active Month.

Each contract's last trading day will be determined by ICE Futures Europe per the WTI Crude Futures contract specification (generally the 4th US business day prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract month, or five US business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a US business day). The last trading day for each contract is posted at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures/expiry.

In the event of a contract specification change, feed change, or similar structural modification affecting the underlying market during the listed time frame, this market will resolve based on adjusted prices as displayed on Pyth.

If the Active Month contract does not trade at all during the listed time frame, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market is Pyth — specifically, the ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures Active Month "High" and "Low" prices available at https://app.pyth.com/explore?search=CLL, with the chart settings configured for 1-minute candles. market.question: Iran charges Hormuz fees by October 31?
market.rules:
This market resolves to “Yes” if the Iranian government officially announces and begins collecting fees, tolls, charges, tariffs, or similar payments from commercial vessels which are mandatory for passage through or access to the Strait of Hormuz between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market resolves to “No.”

A qualifying fee must be an announced policy which applies generally to all commercial vessels, or a defined subcategory of commercial vessels (e.g., vessels flagged to the US and its allies). Isolated demanded charges will not qualify.

A fee is mandatory if, in practice, affected commercial vessels cannot transit or access the Strait of Hormuz without paying it, regardless of whether Iran characterizes the payment as voluntary or a fee for services. Fees described as tolls, maritime fees, service charges, environmental fees, security fees, insurance charges, etc. will qualify provided they are recognized as mandatory for passage through or access to the Strait of Hormuz by a consensus of credible reporting (e.g., a mandatory insurance fee charged by the Iranian Persian Gulf Strait Authority would qualify).

Both of the following are required to occur prior to the specified date, 11:59 PM ET to satisfy this market’s resolution criteria:
1) An official announcement from the Iranian government that such a fee is being, or will be, implemented.
2) A consensus of credible reporting that collection of the fee has begun.

Fees charged by Oman, the United Arab Emirates, shipping insurers, private companies, or other non-Iranian entities do not qualify unless charged jointly with Iran, or if Iran directly receives the fee or controls the charging entity. Normal port fees, customs duties, sanctions-related costs, or shipping surcharges do not alone qualify. 

The resolution sources will be official announcements from the government of Iran and consensus of credible reporting.

recent_facts.fact: NSPM's September poll had Student List at 44.4% and Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia at 41.7%. NSPM's previous poll had them at 39.6% and 37.5%. Four other lists were reported above the 3% threshold.

Faktor plus poll (Sept 16–20, n=986, about 62% expected turnout): United Serbia (SNS) 48.6%, Student List 37.1%, SPS 4.9%, European Serbia 3.6%, Authentic Right 2.8%, Mi snaga naroda 1.2%. 16% of respondents were undecided.
Faktor plus's earlier poll had SNS at 47.2% and Student List at 31.5%. In the next poll the Student List rose 5.6 points and SNS 1.4 points.

All 250 seats are elected by closed-list PR in one nationwide constituency using D'Hondt, with a 3% threshold that is waived for ethnic minority lists. 126 seats are needed for a majority. Sixteen lists were registered, including United Serbia (SNS-led, headed by Vučić), SPS, European Serbia, Authentic Right (NADA) and the Student List (ballot holder Ilija Srdanović).

Aleksandar Vučić resigned as president on September 27, more than seven months before his term ended, after calling the snap election. Al Jazeera reported that polls suggest the race between his party and the student-backed list could be tight.
Vučić launched his campaign for prime minister at Belgrade's largest indoor arena, which thousands of supporters filled, and promised a 'comprehensive' victory.
Vučić dissolved the National Assembly on September 9 and called early elections for October 25, 2026, although the regular mandate ran to December 2027.

Students marched to register the 'Student List – Students Are Winning', a slate of 250 candidates. It is backed by many opposition parties, including DS, ZLF, Kreni-Promeni, SDS, LSV, Dveri and Enough is Enough. Some opposition parties are running separately, for example European Serbia (SSP and others).

In the March 29, 2026 local elections in 10 municipalities, SNS and its partners won all 10 and student-backed lists came second in each. The ruling coalition's share fell compared with the previous elections in 8 of the 10. Examples: Smederevska Palanka, SNS 58% vs. students 29.2%; Aranđelovac, students 46.08% (20 of 41 seats).

Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Prices will be used exactly as published by Pyth, without rounding.

Only prices achieved during an applicable trading session of the specified timeframe's business days will be considered (See: "Trading Hours" at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures). The trading session for a given business day typically begins at 8:00 PM ET on the prior calendar date, except for the session dated Monday, which begins at 6:00 PM ET on the preceding Sunday, and where modified by holiday or other special hours (See: https://www.ice.com/holiday-hours).

The Active Month is the nearest listed contract, except during that contract's final three trading sessions. At the open of the third-to-last trading session, the next listed contract becomes the Active Month.

Each contract's last trading day will be determined by ICE Futures Europe per the WTI Crude Futures contract specification (generally the 4th US business day prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract month, or five US business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a US business day). The last trading day for each contract is posted at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures/expiry.

For example, if the last trading session for the nearest listed contract is the session for Monday the 20th, the next listed contract would become the Active Month at the start of the trading session for Thursday the 16th (8:00 PM ET on Wednesday), assuming a standard trading calendar.

In the event of a contract specification change, feed change, or similar structural modification affecting the underlying market during the listed time frame, this market will resolve based on adjusted prices as displayed on Pyth.

If the Active Month contract does not trade at all during the listed time frame, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market is Pyth — specifically, the ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures Active Month "High" and "Low" prices available at https://app.pyth.com/explore?search=CLL, with the chart settings configured for 1-minute candles. market.question: US announces end of Iranian blockade by October 15, 2026?
market.rules:
On July 13, 2026, Trump announced the United States would reinstate its naval blockade of Iran, targeting Iranian ships and customers.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if the United States government, or an authorized representative of the United States government, publicly and officially announces the end, termination, lifting, or suspension of the United States’ naval blockade on Iranian ships and ships of Iranian customers, between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

An announcement qualifies if it communicates that the United States will generally cease blocking vessel traffic for Iranian ships and customers, including an announcement that the blockade will not take effect at all, even if some restrictions remain (for example, an imposition of fees). An announcement does not qualify if it reflects only a limited or partial change that stops short of a general end or suspension of the blockade, for example, an exemption for a specific vessel, cargo, or port.

A qualifying announcement must be a declarative statement of the United States government’s present termination or suspension of the blockade, previously-unannounced prior termination or suspension of the blockade, or definitive decision to terminate or suspend the blockade.

A qualifying announcement must clearly and unambiguously identify the end or suspension of the blockade. Statements that merely allude to, reference, or describe an end to the blockade, without clearly communicating it, do not qualify. The announcement need not use specific terminology or reference the end of a blockade by name; an announcement of a resumption of prior obligations, the maintenance of a status quo, or a return to a previously agreed baseline qualifies, provided the substantive policy of ending or suspending the blockade is clearly and unambiguously communicated.

A qualifying announcement must be made through official channels, by an individual acting in an official capacity. Statements made incidentally or informally in a context not intended for official communication do not qualify.

The following do not qualify:

Anonymous, unattributed, or leaked statements not confirmed as official;
Statements by persons not authorized to speak for the United States government;
Third-party speculation, analysis, or predictions that the United States government will announce or implement an end to the blockade;
Satirical, fabricated, hacked, or impersonated communications; and
Statements that describe a prospective, contingent, probable, or conditional end to the blockade rather than announcing a present and decided position.

Once a qualifying announcement is made, this market will resolve to “Yes” regardless of whether it is later reversed, or whether the blockade actually ends in practice.

Resolution will be based on official information from the United States government, including the President, the Department of Defense, the Department of State, and United States Central Command (CENTCOM), or the official representatives of the United States government.

recent_facts.fact: On October 2–3, Trump said the Iran war would end "very soon" and "probably right after the midterms" (November 3). The White House said the US is "winning" its economic campaign and that Iranian oil exports have stopped completely because of the blockade.

Iran loaded no crude onto tankers in September 2026, down from about 250,000 barrels per day in August. It was the first month at zero since the war began in February, and the US blockade was still in force.
Trump is sending another aircraft carrier and 10,000 sailors and Marines to the region. Iranian inflation is near 90%, and diplomacy is described as deadlocked.

Trump rejected Iran's proposal for a seven-day ceasefire. Under that proposal, Iran would reopen the Strait of Hormuz and restart talks, and its conditions included lifting the US port blockade, releasing frozen funds and waiving oil sanctions. Trump said "that deal would not be acceptable."

Indirect talks are continuing through Qatari mediators. Foreign Minister Araghchi expected a formal US response by about September 29. A US official called the talks "positive and constructive" but said there would be no deal unless the nuclear issues are addressed. Trump said "I offered them NOTHING" in reply to reports of possible sanctions relief.
Reports say Trump told aides he expects to resume bombing Iran after the November 3 midterm elections if negotiations fail.

On October 4, Iranian parliament speaker Ghalibaf said the strait will stay closed until Iran's conditions are met. The report says Tehran wants a deal before the November 3 election, while Trump talks of ending the war after it.
Axios reported that envoys Witkoff and Kushner and Vice President Vance still believed diplomacy was worth pursuing, while Trump appeared much more skeptical.

After talks around the UN General Assembly, Trump called the discussions "very good" but demanded better terms than Iran had offered. Treasury added sanctions on Iranian railway and automotive firms on October 1.

recent_facts.source: Wikipedia (2026 US naval blockade of Iran) / NPR
recent_facts.fact: The first blockade phase began on April 13, 2026. It ended after a deal was announced on June 14 and signed at Versailles on June 17, and CENTCOM announced the blockade's removal on June 18, about 66 days in. Removal came only as part of a signed ceasefire agreement that started a 60-day negotiation period.

recent_facts.source: Wikipedia (2026 US naval blockade of Iran)
recent_facts.fact: Trump announced on July 13 that the blockade would be reinstated, and it resumed on July 14–15. CENTCOM reported 55 vessels redirected by August 11 and more than 100 by September 12. The page records no announcement about ending the blockade from August through early October.

The last time the blockade was lifted, the official announcement came from CENTCOM after a signed US–Iran memorandum. That is the kind of official-channel, general lifting the resolution rules require; an exemption for a specific vessel or cargo would not count.

The key upcoming date is the US midterm election on November 3, 2026, which falls after both closing dates (October 15 and October 31). No formal US–Iran negotiating round had been publicly scheduled as of October 4.

Iran loaded no crude onto tankers in September 2026, down from about 250,000 barrels per day in August. It was the first month at zero since the war began in February, and the US blockade was still in force.
Trump is sending another aircraft carrier and 10,000 sailors and Marines to the region. Iranian inflation is near 90%, and diplomacy is described as deadlocked.

Trump rejected Iran's proposal for a seven-day ceasefire. Under that proposal, Iran would reopen the Strait of Hormuz and restart talks, and its conditions included lifting the US port blockade, releasing frozen funds and waiving oil sanctions. Trump said "that deal would not be acceptable."

Indirect talks are continuing through Qatari mediators. Foreign Minister Araghchi expected a formal US response by about September 29. A US official called the talks "positive and constructive" but said there would be no deal unless the nuclear issues are addressed. Trump said "I offered them NOTHING" in reply to reports of possible sanctions relief.
Reports say Trump told aides he expects to resume bombing Iran after the November 3 midterm elections if negotiations fail.

On October 4, Iranian parliament speaker Ghalibaf said the strait will stay closed until Iran's conditions are met. The report says Tehran wants a deal before the November 3 election, while Trump talks of ending the war after it.
Axios reported that envoys Witkoff and Kushner and Vice President Vance still believed diplomacy was worth pursuing, while Trump appeared much more skeptical.

After talks around the UN General Assembly, Trump called the discussions "very good" but demanded better terms than Iran had offered. Treasury added sanctions on Iranian railway and automotive firms on October 1.

recent_facts.fact: The first blockade phase began on April 13, 2026. It ended after a deal was announced on June 14 and signed at Versailles on June 17, and CENTCOM announced the blockade's removal on June 18, about 66 days in. Removal came only as part of a signed ceasefire agreement that started a 60-day negotiation period.

recent_facts.source: Wikipedia (2026 US naval blockade of Iran)
recent_facts.fact: Trump announced on July 13 that the blockade would be reinstated, and it resumed on July 14–15. CENTCOM reported 55 vessels redirected by August 11 and more than 100 by September 12. The page records no announcement about ending the blockade from August through early October.

The last time the blockade was lifted, the official announcement came from CENTCOM after a signed US–Iran memorandum. That is the kind of official-channel, general lifting the resolution rules require; an exemption for a specific vessel or cargo would not count.

The key upcoming date is the US midterm election on November 3, 2026, which falls after both closing dates (October 15 and October 31). No formal US–Iran negotiating round had been publicly scheduled as of October 4.

market.question: Will there be no change in Fed interest rates after the October 2026 meeting?
market.rules:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's October 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for October 27-28, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their October meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

recent_facts.fact: The FOMC unanimously raised rates by 25 bp to 3.75–4.00% on September 16, 2026, its first hike since 2023. Three members had favored a hike at the July meeting. The September dot plot's median shows one more 25 bp hike in 2026, ending the year at about 4.1%.

Vice Chair Philip Jefferson and New York Fed President John Williams said in separate speeches that the Fed has time to assess the economy before considering another rate increase. These remarks were reported as reducing investor expectations of an October hike.
A Bloomberg report published October 2 had the headline 'Fed may skip October but pull U.S. rate hike trigger in December'.

In late September, before the weak jobs data: Williams (Sept 24) called another hike before year-end 'reasonable'. Paulson (Sept 24) said further hikes may be needed. Hammack (Sept 25) warned an 'inflationary mindset could start to set in'. Governor Cook (Sept 28) said the labor market 'appears to be well positioned to handle an increase in rates'.

Warsh described the September move as having 'removed a dose of accommodation'. He has avoided signaling where rates go next. Higher energy prices tied to the Iran war were cited as one reason for the hike.
September 2026 CPI is due October 14, 2026 at 8:30 a.m. ET, before the FOMC meeting. September PCE is due later in October.

Aaron Judge was left off the Yankees' ALDS roster with a moderate right calf (soleus) strain he suffered Sept 16. He played only 66 games in 2026. Boone said keeping him off was meant to help get a version of Judge back to win a World Series, which suggests a possible return in a later round.

market.rules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if, at any point after market creation and during a trading session of October 2026, any Pyth 1-minute candle for the Active Month of ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures (denoted by Pyth as "CLL") has a final "High" or "Low" price equal to or beyond (above for ↑ High Prices, below for ↓ Low Prices) the listed price. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Prices will be used exactly as published by Pyth, without rounding.

Only prices achieved during an applicable trading session of the specified timeframe's business days will be considered (See: "Trading Hours" at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures). The trading session for a given business day typically begins at 8:00 PM ET on the prior calendar date, except for the session dated Monday, which begins at 6:00 PM ET on the preceding Sunday, and where modified by holiday or other special hours (See: https://www.ice.com/holiday-hours).

The Active Month is the nearest listed contract, except during that contract's final three trading sessions. At the open of the third-to-last trading session, the next listed contract becomes the Active Month.

Each contract's last trading day will be determined by ICE Futures Europe per the WTI Crude Futures contract specification (generally the 4th US business day prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract month, or five US business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a US business day). The last trading day for each contract is posted at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures/expiry.

For example, if the last trading session for the nearest listed contract is the session for Monday the 20th, the next listed contract would become the Active Month at the start of the trading session for Thursday the 16th (8:00 PM ET on Wednesday), assuming a standard trading calendar.

If the relevant Pyth data is unavailable due to a system outage, data failure, or other disruption that prevents verification of the required 1-minute candle data, the official daily high/low price published for the Active Month WTI Crude Oil Futures contract by ICE Futures Europe may be used to determine whether the listed price was reached during the applicable trading session (See: https://www.ice.com/report/10 with "T-West Texas Intermediate Light Sweet Crude Future" selected).

In the event of a contract specification change, feed change, or similar structural modification affecting the underlying market during the listed time frame, this market will resolve based on adjusted prices as displayed on Pyth.

If the Active Month contract does not trade at all during the listed time frame, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market is Pyth — specifically, the ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures Active Month "High" and "Low" prices available at https://app.pyth.com/explore?search=CLL, with the chart settings configured for 1-minute candles. This market will resolve to the electoral list that wins the greatest number of seats in the National Assembly of Serbia as a result of this election.

Electoral lists will be primarily ranked by the number of seats won in the specified election. If two or more lists are tied on seats, ties will be broken by the total number of valid votes received, with higher vote totals ranking higher. If lists remain tied, ties will be broken by alphabetical order of the listed names. This market will resolve to the list that occupies the highest finishing position after applying this ranking.

If the results of the specified election are not definitively known by March 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

recent_facts.fact: OpenAI cancelled the release of its Astra 6.1 model on safety grounds. The model had been due to launch in October 2026 in ChatGPT and Codex.

market.question: Saudi Oil Pipeline (East-West) restarts by October 15?
market.rules:
On September 11, 2026, Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Energy announced that the East-West oil pipeline has been shut down.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if the government of Saudi Arabia announces that the East-West oil pipeline is operational or no longer shut down between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A qualifying announcement must express that the pipeline is presently operating; operation at partial or reduced capacity qualifies.

Announcements that attribute such a claim to third parties, state that the pipeline will or may operate in the future, describe work underway to restore operation, or frame resumption as expected, planned, or conditional, will not qualify.

Once a qualifying announcement is made, this market will resolve to “Yes,” regardless of any subsequent contradictory statements, or alternative information from other sources.

The resolution source for this market will be official information from the government of Saudi Arabia.

recent_facts.fact: The East-West pipeline restarted on September 22, 2026 at a low rate, with Aramco working to bring flows back to about 4 million bpd. The report rests on Reuters sources and does not cite any announcement from the Saudi government, the Ministry of Energy or SPA.

Saudi Aramco is reported to be pumping close to 6 million bpd through the 7 million bpd East-West pipeline, more than 80% of capacity, after the September 22 restart. The report notes that Aramco and the Saudi energy ministry did not respond to requests for comment, so no official confirmation is cited. Date approximate (early October).

The Ministry of Energy said the East–West pipeline was shut down as a precaution after multiple drone attacks launched from Iraq on September 10–11. The attacks hit the Riyadh and Medina regions, causing fires, some damage and injuries.
US Energy Secretary Chris Wright told CNBC the Saudi pipeline closure would be a brief interruption lasting days. This is a US official speaking, not the Saudi government.

The 7 million bpd pipeline carries crude to Red Sea export terminals and has been Saudi Arabia's main way around Hormuz during the Iran war. Brent rose more than 3% to $108 after the shutdown. Later reports said Yanbu loadings had picked up, a sign the pipeline was running again.

recent_facts.source: Saudi Press Agency / Al Jazeera / Fortune
recent_facts.fact: Precedent: after the earlier 2026 attacks cut East-West throughput by about 700,000 bpd, the Ministry of Energy issued an SPA statement on April 12, 2026 saying full pumping capacity of about 7 million bpd had been restored, along with 300,000 bpd at Manifa. That was an official, public restoration announcement within days of the damage.

SPA headline: 'Ministry of Energy: Energy Facilities and East–West Pipeline Affected by the Attacks Have Recovered and Restored Operational Capacity'. Coverage dates this statement to April 12, 2026, which is before the September shutdown and outside the market window. The page shows no date, so the date is inferred from news coverage. One search summary attributed a similar ministry statement to September 29, 2026, but this could not be confirmed and is probably confused with the April statement.

The question closes October 15, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. Only an official Saudi government statement that the pipeline is operating now counts, and partial capacity is enough. Reports from Reuters, Bloomberg or Kpler sources, and statements about future resumption, do not count.

market.question: Will the Rhine River return to normal levels between October 1 and October 31, 2026?
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the date (Berlin time) when the water level at the Kaub gauge (station 25700100) on the Rhine River first reaches or exceeds 77 centimeters, as reported by the German Federal Waterways and Shipping Administration (WSV) via PegelOnline.

A reading of 77 centimeters or higher is the equivalent water level (Gleichwertiger Wasserstand, GlW) for Kaub, the low-water reference mark below which shipping becomes structurally disrupted, and defines "normal levels" for this market.

The resolution is triggered by the first reading at or above 77 centimeters recorded on or after the market's start, representing a rise back to the threshold. A single reading at or above 77 centimeters is sufficient to trigger resolution; transient spikes count, and the water level does not need to be sustained at or above 77 centimeters for any period.

If readings for timestamps on or after November 1, 2026 (Berlin time) are available on the resolution source, and no reading at or above 77 centimeters has been recorded for a timestamp before November 1, 2026 (Berlin time), this market will resolve to "No return before November 1, 2026." If readings for timestamps on or after November 1, 2026 (Berlin time) have not been recorded on the resolution source by November 2, 2026, 11:59 PM Berlin time, and no reading at or above 77 centimeters has been recorded for a timestamp before November 1, 2026 (Berlin time), this market will resolve to "No return before November 1, 2026."

The resolution source for this market will be PegelOnline (https://www.pegelonline.wsv.de/gast/stammdaten?pegelnr=25700100).

recent_facts.fact: ELWIS currently lists these Kaub reference levels: GlW = 77 cm, M_I = 460 cm, M_II/HSW = 640 cm. Older sources cite 78 cm as Kaub's critical low-water mark.
Kaub fell to -6 cm on October 1, 2026, below the gauge zero. Riviera rerouted cruises because ships could not get through the Rhine Gorge.

Kaub ranged between -6 cm and +5 cm over the week to early October. It rose 3 cm to -1 cm on October 2 after 9.1 mm of Alpine rain, against a normal 3.1 mm. The site calls this the lowest season in 30 years of its records.
Kaub measured 9 cm on October 4, up 13 cm over the previous 72 hours. The same source says a normal October at Kaub runs about 100–205 cm.
Reports said the rain in the first week of October lifted the Rhine only slightly, by a few centimetres. Weather models showed mostly dry, mild autumn weather for the first half of October.

Weather outlooks say Oct 7–15 will bring repeated showers rather than widespread steady rain. They show wetter, cooler weather from mid-October, with noticeable rain possible in the south and in the Alps, partly as snow at altitude, while the north stays drier.
In late September 2026, Kaub dropped below 0 cm. The report calls this the first time the gauge has gone negative.
Rhine shipping stalled in August 2026 when Kaub hit a record low. Reports put that low at about 5 cm, so the low-water period has lasted since at least mid-August.

In 2018, Kaub stayed below 78 cm for more than 130 straight days between July and December, bottoming at 25 cm on October 22, 2018. It did not regain 78 cm in October that year. This is a single comparable case, and the counts are unverified.

In 2022, Kaub dropped below 30 cm in August and recovered to workable levels by late September. This is a single comparable case and is unverified. Its low point (about 30 cm) was far above the current 2026 levels of around 0–9 cm.

Only prices achieved during an applicable trading session of the specified timeframe's business days will be considered (See: "Trading Hours" at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures). The Active Month is the nearest listed contract, except during that contract's final three trading sessions. At the open of the third-to-last trading session, the next listed contract becomes the Active Month.

A general statement that it was conducted by an Iranian proxy will also qualify, even if no group is named.

Such a statement will be considered to claim that Iran or its affiliated groups deliberately caused the incident if it explicitly claims that Iran or an affiliated group ordered, carried out, planned, or otherwise directly aided or coordinated the incident. Statements that attribute only inspiration or ideological influence (e.g., "this would not have happened if Iran didn't radicalize terrorists," "the co-pilot was influenced by Hamas' ideas") will not qualify.

Once a qualifying announcement has been made, no subsequent walkback or retraction will be relevant for purposes of this market.

Israeli officials said they currently had no signs of Iranian involvement. An Israeli intelligence official said: "We don't know yet if he is a 'lone wolf' or whether he was sent by someone to conduct an attack." Defense Minister Israel Katz called it a terrorist attack.

Netanyahu said the Omani co-pilot "underwent Islamist radical indoctrination" and was suicidal, and said this came from the co-pilot's personal information. He did not name Iran or any proxy group as having directed the attack.

Reports say al-Hammami posted pro-Hamas, anti-Israel content on social media. Investigators reportedly think an operation like this would have needed outside help with planning and logistics. The UAE and Israel are investigating jointly.

Al Jazeera said there was no official confirmation of the co-pilot's identity or beliefs. UAE investigators are checking whether he acted as a lone wolf or had links to extremist groups. The WSJ reported that Oman had earlier barred him from flying over concerns about extremist views.

recent_facts.fact: Reports say al-Hammami was radicalized while in Syria, and extremist material was found on him in 2024 while he worked for Oman Air. The Australian Federal Police are looking into whether he was radicalized while studying in Australia in 2015–2017.

Saudi Arabia's first assessment found the assailant meant to crash the plane but could not establish a motive or whether he acted alone. recent_facts.source: The Globe and Mail / Irish Times

In the upcoming game, scheduled for October 10, 2026
If FC Barcelona wins, this market will resolve to "Yes".
Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".
If the game is postponed, this market will remain open until the game has been completed.
If the game is canceled entirely, with no make-up game, this market will resolve "No".
This market refers only to the outcome within the first 90 minutes of regular play plus stoppage time.

The primary resolution source for this market is the official statistics of the event as recognized by the governing body or event organizers. However, if the governing body or event organizers have not published final match statistics within 2 hours after the event's conclusion, data from Flashscore may be used; if Flashscore data is unavailable, data from Sofascore may be used; if neither is available, a consensus of credible reporting may be used instead. All markets will settle based on the official final result as recognized by the governing body or event organizers. Revisions to officially declared final scores made after market resolution will not be accounted for in determining the outcome. If no acceptable data is available within 24 hours of the event's conclusion, this market will resolve 50-50, or to "Draw" where applicable.

market.question: Saudi Oil Pipeline (East-West) restarts by October 31?
market.rules:
On September 11, 2026, Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Energy announced that the East-West oil pipeline has been shut down.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if the government of Saudi Arabia announces that the East-West oil pipeline is operational or no longer shut down between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A qualifying announcement must express that the pipeline is presently operating; operation at partial or reduced capacity qualifies.

Announcements that attribute such a claim to third parties, state that the pipeline will or may operate in the future, describe work underway to restore operation, or frame resumption as expected, planned, or conditional, will not qualify.

Once a qualifying announcement is made, this market will resolve to “Yes,” regardless of any subsequent contradictory statements, or alternative information from other sources.

The resolution source for this market will be official information from the government of Saudi Arabia.

recent_facts.fact: The East-West pipeline restarted on September 22, 2026 at a low rate, with Aramco working to bring flows back to about 4 million bpd. The report rests on Reuters sources and does not cite any announcement from the Saudi government, the Ministry of Energy or SPA.

Saudi Aramco is reported to be pumping close to 6 million bpd through the 7 million bpd East-West pipeline, more than 80% of capacity, after the September 22 restart. The report notes that Aramco and the Saudi energy ministry did not respond to requests for comment, so no official confirmation is cited. Date approximate (early October).

The Ministry of Energy said the East–West pipeline was shut down as a precaution after multiple drone attacks launched from Iraq on September 10–11. The attacks hit the Riyadh and Medina regions, causing fires, some damage and injuries.
US Energy Secretary Chris Wright told CNBC the Saudi pipeline closure would be a brief interruption lasting days. This is a US official speaking, not the Saudi government.

The 7 million bpd pipeline carries crude to Red Sea export terminals and has been Saudi Arabia's main way around Hormuz during the Iran war. Brent rose more than 3% to $108 after the shutdown. Later reports said Yanbu loadings had picked up, a sign the pipeline was running again.

recent_facts.source: Saudi Press Agency / Al Jazeera / Fortune
recent_facts.fact: Precedent: after the earlier 2026 attacks cut East-West throughput by about 700,000 bpd, the Ministry of Energy issued an SPA statement on April 12, 2026 saying full pumping capacity of about 7 million bpd had been restored, along with 300,000 bpd at Manifa. That was an official, public restoration announcement within days of the damage.

SPA headline: 'Ministry of Energy: Energy Facilities and East–West Pipeline Affected by the Attacks Have Recovered and Restored Operational Capacity'. Coverage dates this statement to April 12, 2026, which is before the September shutdown and outside the market window. The page shows no date, so the date is inferred from news coverage. One search summary attributed a similar ministry statement to September 29, 2026, but this could not be confirmed and is probably confused with the April statement.

The question closes October 15, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. Only an official Saudi government statement that the pipeline is operating now counts, and partial capacity is enough. Reports from Reuters, Bloomberg or Kpler sources, and statements about future resumption, do not count.

It quotes no Saudi government statement saying the pipeline is operating again.

market.question: Will WTI Crude Oil (WTI) hit (LOW) $85 in October?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if, at any point after market creation and during a trading session of October 2026, any Pyth 1-minute candle for the Active Month of ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures (denoted by Pyth as "CLL") has a final "High" or "Low" price equal to or beyond (above for ↑ High Prices, below for ↓ Low Prices) the listed price. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Prices will be used exactly as published by Pyth, without rounding.

Only prices achieved during an applicable trading session of the specified timeframe's business days will be considered (See: "Trading Hours" at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures). The trading session for a given business day typically begins at 8:00 PM ET on the prior calendar date, except for the session dated Monday, which begins at 6:00 PM ET on the preceding Sunday, and where modified by holiday or other special hours (See: https://www.ice.com/holiday-hours).

The Active Month is the nearest listed contract, except during that contract's final three trading sessions. At the open of the third-to-last trading session, the next listed contract becomes the Active Month.

Each contract's last trading day will be determined by ICE Futures Europe per the WTI Crude Futures contract specification (generally the 4th US business day prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract month, or five US business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a US business day). The last trading day for each contract is posted at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures/expiry.

For example, if the last trading session for the nearest listed contract is the session for Monday the 20th, the next listed contract would become the Active Month at the start of the trading session for Thursday the 16th (8:00 PM ET on Wednesday), assuming a standard trading calendar.

If the relevant Pyth data is unavailable due to a system outage, data failure, or other disruption that prevents verification of the required 1-minute candle data, the official daily high/low price published for the Active Month WTI Crude Oil Futures contract by ICE Futures Europe may be used to determine whether the listed price was reached during the applicable trading session (See: https://www.ice.com/report/10 with "T-West Texas Intermediate Light Sweet Crude Future" selected).

In the event of a contract specification change, feed change, or similar structural modification affecting the underlying market during the listed time frame, this market will resolve based on adjusted prices as displayed on Pyth.

If the Active Month contract does not trade at all during the listed time frame, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market is Pyth — specifically, the ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures Active Month "High" and "Low" prices available at https://app.pyth.com/explore?search=CLL, with the chart settings configured for 1-minute candles. Historical 1-minute candles may be accessed by appending a Unix timestamp (seconds) to the Pyth chart URL using the "t=" parameter.

market.question: 2026 Balance of Power: D Senate, D House
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the party that wins control of the United States Senate and the party that wins control of the United States House of Representatives in the 2026 United States midterm election.

A party wins control of the United States Senate if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the party that wins control of the chamber is the party that wins half of the voting seats and holds the Vice Presidency. If the outcome remains ambiguous after applying the above criteria, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first selected President Pro Tempore of the Congress that convenes after the specified election is affiliated.

A party wins control of the United States House of Representatives if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first elected Speaker of the House of the Congress that convenes after the 2026 midterm election is affiliated.

The following rules govern the counting of seats for determining which party wins control of the chambers.

For determining Senate control, all regular and special Senate elections that determine representation in the upcoming 120th Congress and are scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026 are included. Vacant Senate seats for which no election or special election to fill the seat is scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026 will be treated as held by the party affiliation of the most recent member to hold that seat. For determining House control, all House elections in the 2026 United States midterm election that elect voting members and determine representation in the upcoming 120th Congress are included. Where a Senate or House seat is decided by a runoff, the runoff result will determine attribution of that seat, even if it takes place after November 2026.

For seats contested in the specified election, seats are attributed to the party under which the member was elected. If a member-elect changes party affiliation, or vacates their seat, between election day and the formal organization of Congress, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was elected. 

For seats not contested in the specified election, seats are attributed to the party that holds the seat as of the date of the election. If a current sitting member of the U.S. Senate who is not up for election changes party affiliation or vacates their seat after the date of the election, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was affiliated at the time of the election.

Senate and House members elected as independents who formally caucus with, or, for newly elected members, who announce their intent to caucus with, a party are included in that party’s count. If the caucus decisions of members of the Senate or House elected as independents cannot be determined on the date of the election, this market may remain open until the earlier of (i) an announcement from the relevant members of their intents to caucus, or (ii) January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year. If no such announcement is made by January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year, the member will not count towards the seat count of any party.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from relevant state electoral authorities, the United States Congress, and a consensus of credible reporting.

In October 2026, Trump's approval averages 37.3% approve and 60.3% disapprove (net -23.0), with individual trackers ranging from 34% to 39% approve. His approval among independents is 34%, below the 36% seen before Democrats gained 41 seats in 2018.
One month before the midterms, Trump's approval is underwater in 39 states and in every major battleground state.

The president's party has lost House seats in 18 of the 20 midterms since 1946, with an average loss of about 25 to 26 seats. The two exceptions were 1998 (Democrats +5) and 2002 (Republicans +8). The publication date shown is approximate.

When the president's approval was below 50%, his party lost an average of 37 House seats in midterms, compared with an average of 14 when approval was above 50%. This covers data through 2014 only; the publication date shown is approximate.

Mid-decade redistricting moved seats in both directions: Texas about +5 for Republicans, California about +5 for Democrats, Missouri +1 R, North Carolina +1 R and Ohio +2 R. Accounts put the overall net Republican gain from redistricting at about 5 to 8 seats.

In the Louisiana (Callais) case, the Supreme Court struck down Louisiana's map as a racial gerrymander, weakening the Voting Rights Act. Afterward, Louisiana, Alabama, Florida and Tennessee enacted new maps.
Louisiana approved a new map that eliminates one majority-Black district, which would change the delegation from 4R-2D to 5R-1D. The date shown is approximate.

On September 25, 2026, the Cook Political Report moved 15 House races toward Democrats. AZ-1 and NJ-7 went from Toss-up to Lean Democrat, and three seats, including TX-15 (De La Cruz), went from Likely Republican to Toss-up. Cook now rates 23 races as Toss-ups: 17 held by Republicans and 5 by Democrats.

market.question: Will the Democratic Party control the Senate after the 2026 Midterm elections?
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the party that wins control of the United States Senate in the 2026 United States midterm election.

A party wins control of the United States Senate if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the party that wins control of the chamber is the party that wins half of the voting seats and holds the Vice Presidency. If the outcome remains ambiguous after applying the above criteria, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first selected President Pro Tempore of the Congress that convenes after the specified election is affiliated.

The following rules govern the counting of seats for determining which party wins control of the chamber.

All regular and special Senate elections that determine representation in the upcoming 120th Congress and are scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026 are included. Runoffs for qualifying elections will determine attribution of the relevant seat, even if they take place after November 2026. Vacant seats for which no election or special election to fill the seat is scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026 will be treated as held by the party affiliation of the most recent member to hold that seat.

For seats contested in the specified election, seats are attributed to the party under which the member was elected. If a member-elect changes party affiliation, or vacates their seat, between election day and the formal organization of Congress, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was elected.

For seats not contested in the specified election, seats are attributed to the party that holds the seat as of the date of the election. If a current sitting member of the U.S. Senate who is not up for election changes party affiliation or vacates their seat after the date of the election, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was affiliated at the time of the election.

Senate members elected as independents who formally caucus with, or, for newly elected members, who announce their intent to caucus with, a party are included in that party’s count. If the caucus decisions of members of the Senate elected as independents cannot be determined on the date of the election, this market may remain open until the earlier of (i) an announcement from the relevant members of their intents to caucus, or (ii) January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year. If no such announcement is made by January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year, the member will not count towards the seat count of any party.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from relevant state electoral authorities, the United States Congress, and a consensus of credible reporting.

recent_facts.source: Wikipedia (2026 United States Senate election in South Carolina)
recent_facts.fact: Lindsey Graham won the June 9 GOP primary and then died of cardiac arrest on July 11, 2026. Gov. McMaster appointed his sister Darline Graham to the seat on July 13. She won the special GOP runoff on Aug 25 against Rep. Ralph Norman with 52.5%, so she is the Republican nominee.

recent_facts.source: Wikipedia (2026 United States Senate election in South Carolina)
recent_facts.fact: Pediatrician Annie Andrews is the Democratic nominee. She beat Brandon Brown in the primary with 61.5%.

An InsiderAdvantage poll (Sept 28-29, 1,200 likely voters, MoE ±2.83) had Darline Graham (R) at 46% and Andrews (D) at 45%, with other candidates at 5% and 4% undecided. Mark Hackett (Constitution) had 3% and Kasie Whitener (Libertarian) had 2%.
A Trafalgar Group poll (Sept 23-25, 1,087 likely voters, MoE ±2.9) had Graham at 43.4% and Andrews at 42.3%, with 8.5% undecided. An earlier InsiderAdvantage poll (Sept 8-9) had Graham ahead 45%-43%.
Rasmussen Reports had Graham ahead of Andrews 48% to 43%.
PollingSource's average of 3 polls from the last 30 days shows Graham at 44.7% and Andrews at 42.3%, a Republican lead of 2.4 points.

Cook Political Report moved the SC Senate race from Solid Republican to Likely Republican. It cited Darline Graham's uneven debate performance and possible backlash over being elevated because of her family name. Newsweek (Oct 2) lists Sabato's Crystal Ball at Safe Republican.

Andrews is outraising and outspending Graham. Spending on the Democratic side is about $5.1M against about $4.9M on the Republican side, and Andrews' campaign says it accounts for about 96% of ad spending. Graham had about $250K left before the Sept 30 reporting deadline, and the American Mission super PAC reported nearly $500K in September support for her.
No Democrat has won a statewide election in South Carolina since Jim Rex in 2006. In 2020, Democrat Jaime Harrison lost to Lindsey Graham by about 10 points.

Final 2020 polls showed a close race: Data for Progress (Oct 27-Nov 1) had Graham ahead 49-46, and Morning Consult (Oct 22-31) had him ahead 46-44. Lindsey Graham won by about 10 points, so the polls understated the Republican margin by roughly 6-8 points.
Unverified, recalled from memory: the last Democrat to win a U.S. Senate race in South Carolina was Fritz Hollings in 1998. Republicans have won every SC Senate election since then.

recent_facts.fact: The general election is on November 3, 2026, and the Constitution and Libertarian parties also have nominees on the ballot. The question resolves once AP, Fox News and NBC all call the race for the same candidate; otherwise it resolves on official certification.

recent_facts.fact: Abdul El-Sayed won the August 4, 2026 Michigan Democratic Senate primary with 48.5%, beating Rep. Haley Stevens (Mallory McMorrow had withdrawn in July). He is the Democratic nominee against Republican former Rep. Mike Rogers in the open seat being left by retiring Sen. Gary Peters.
Fox News poll of Michigan likely voters, fielded September 24-28, 2026: El-Sayed (D) 50%, Rogers (R) 49%.
Marist poll fielded September 24-27, 2026: El-Sayed 51%, Rogers 44% among registered voters (a 7-point lead).
Rasmussen Reports survey of 1,099 Michigan likely voters, conducted September 22, 2026: El-Sayed 47%, Rogers 44%.

Washington Post-Schar School telephone poll of 803 Michigan likely voters, September 10-14, 2026: El-Sayed 48%, Rogers 45% (margin of error ±3.9). The Post described the national environment as heavily favoring Democrats.
Emerson/Nexstar poll of 1,000 Michigan likely voters, September 12-14, 2026: El-Sayed 48%, Rogers 46%, 4% undecided, 2% another candidate.
A Glengariff (GLCF) poll reported in late September 2026 showed a dead heat between Rogers and El-Sayed. A Breitbart article dated 2026-09-25 also reported a poll with Rogers leading.
The RealClearPolling polling average as of about October 4, 2026 was El-Sayed 47.9%, Rogers 44.3%, an El-Sayed lead of about 3.6 points.
An earlier Fox News poll of 1,006 Michigan registered voters, August 6-10, 2026, had Rogers 51%, El-Sayed 47%. In that poll Trump's favorability in Michigan was 40% favorable and 59% unfavorable.
Cook Political Report rates the Michigan Senate race a Toss-up. It is the only Democratic-held seat Cook rates that way.

Disclosed spending in the race has passed $205 million. Outside spending favors Rogers at about $89 million, against about $46 million for El-Sayed, and another $65 million in ads is reserved through Election Day.
As of July 15, El-Sayed's campaign had raised $14.5 million, $3.7 million more than Rogers. About 450 donors had given El-Sayed the maximum, versus about 150 for Rogers.
Two televised debates between El-Sayed and Rogers are scheduled: October 8 on WOOD-TV (7-8 p.m.) and October 21 on WXYZ-TV Detroit, broadcast statewide. Election Day is November 3, 2026.

Republicans have not won a Michigan U.S. Senate race since 1994 and have not won this seat since 1972. Unverified figures from memory: Democrats won the 2024 Michigan Senate race by about 0.3 points (Slotkin over Rogers) and the 2020 race by about 1.7 points (Peters).
Michigan has no runoff, so the plurality winner takes the seat. The general election ballot also includes Libertarian, Green, U.S. Taxpayers and Natural Law nominees.

In the reverse fixture on 2026-09-29 in Sevilla, Spain beat Croatia 4-1. Lamine Yamal scored twice and Marc Pubill and Nico Williams added one each; Dion Beljo's header had briefly made it 1-1.

market.rules:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if IMF PortWatch publishes a 7-day moving average of transit calls (“Arrivals of Ships”) for the Bab el-Mandeb Strait less than or equal to 10 for any date between market creation and the listed date. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

This market will resolve as soon as IMF PortWatch publishes a 7-day moving average of transit calls for the Bab el-Mandeb Strait equal to or below 10, or once data has been published for the listed date and no such value has been published.

If no data has been published for the listed date within 14 calendar days (ET) after that date, this market will resolve based on the data published up to that point.

Revisions to previously published data points made before data has been published for the listed date will be considered; however, they will not disqualify a previously published data point from qualifying. Revisions made after data has been published for the listed date will not be considered.

The resolution source for this market will be IMF PortWatch, specifically the “Arrivals of Ships” data published for the Bab el-Mandeb Strait at https://portwatch.imf.org/pages/6b1814d64903461b98144a6cc25eb79c.

recent_facts.fact: According to IMF PortWatch, Bab el-Mandeb traffic averaged 28 vessels/day in August 2026, the lowest monthly level in the recent series. A 3-day sample to about 11 September averaged about 26/day (79 vessels), and the 7-day moving average was 24/day on 29 July.

A late-September update said IMF PortWatch recorded a single transit for 20 September, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85/day. It did not say whether this was a preliminary or lagged figure, and it gave no 7-day average. Neither the figure nor which strait it refers to has been checked against PortWatch.

recent_facts.source: Search summary of late-September shipping reports (unverified)
recent_facts.fact: Reports summarized in search results said IMF PortWatch AIS data for Bab el-Mandeb in mid-to-late September 2026 showed daily volumes in the low-to-mid 20s, with about 22 vessels on recent days. This has not been checked against the PortWatch page itself.

Lloyd's List Intelligence's own Red Sea Transit Monitor counted 290 preliminary Bab el-Mandeb transits for 21–27 September 2026 (264 the week before), a 4-week weekly average of 280, against 316 in June and 257 in January. This counting method differs from PortWatch's and gives higher numbers.
In early to mid September 2026, the Houthis seized Yemen's Red Sea coast down to the Bab el-Mandeb, including the port of Mocha. Other reports say they also took Perim Island and the Hanish Islands.
Windward reported that Bab el-Mandeb traffic fell from 35 daily transits before the Houthi advance to 25 after. Traffic then recovered, reaching 45 transits on one Sunday in mid-September.

The Houthis attacked Saudi Arabia's East-West crude pipeline in September 2026 and said Saudi shipping using the strait would be targeted. There have been 12 Houthi attacks or attempted attacks on commercial vessels in the southern Red Sea since July 2026.
The Houthis told the EU in a letter that they would not target European ships in the Red Sea and that their activity would not affect navigation through Bab el-Mandeb.

On 4 October 2026, the Saudi-led coalition pledged support for a Yemeni government offensive against the Houthis. ABC News reported the same day that the Houthis targeted a Saudi oil facility as hostilities escalated.

The Houthi blockade on Saudi Arabia, imposed on 20 July 2026, reduced crude exports through the Yanbu terminals. The Saudi pipeline has resumed at reduced rates, and some operators are increasingly sending ships back through the Red Sea.
A Houthi missile attack on the Egyptian cargo ship Tihamah in the Bab el-Mandeb on 11 August 2026 killed four to six crew. The PortWatch monthly average stayed at 28/day for August.

recent_facts.source: Anadolu Agency (citing IMF PortWatch / World Bank)
recent_facts.fact: PortWatch daily averages: about 71/day from January 2022 to October 2023; 43/day from 17 November 2023 to 19 February 2024; about 33.5/day in 2025; 34–37/day in January–July 2026; 28/day in August 2026. None of the figures found here comes close to a 7-day average of 10 or below, including through the 2024–2025 Houthi campaign. This is not a full check of PortWatch's daily series.

The question resolves Yes if PortWatch publishes a 7-day moving average of Bab el-Mandeb transit calls of 10 or below for any date through 31 October 2026. market.question: Saudi-Houthi ceasefire agreement announced by October 31?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if a ceasefire agreement between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis is announced by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A ceasefire agreement refers to any mutually-agreed suspension of direct military engagement between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis. A broader peace deal, normalization agreement, political framework, truce, or humanitarian pause will qualify if it includes a mutually agreed suspension of direct military engagement, to be effective on a specified date. Agreements that outline future negotiations or de-escalation measures without an explicit, dated commitment to stop fighting will not qualify. Any form of informal understanding, backchannel communication, de-escalation without an announced agreement, or unilateral pause in hostilities will not be considered a ceasefire agreement. Only agreements which constitute a general pause in the conflict will qualify. Agreements which only apply to specific conflict categories (e.g. restrictions on certain target categories or certain locations) will not qualify.

All listed countries/parties must announce their acceptance of the same qualifying diplomatic agreement for a Yes resolution. A joint announcement will qualify, as will separate announcements from each entity of its own acceptance of an agreement which, taken together, directly indicate that all the listed countries accepted the same agreement. Separate announcements of individual policies will not qualify if the policies are not announced as part of a diplomatic agreement.

Each announcement must be a declarative statement that clearly and unambiguously communicates acceptance of an agreement. Statements that reference ongoing negotiations or a prospective agreement, or that allude to or express support for an agreement without confirming acceptance of the agreement, do not qualify. A qualifying announcement need not reference the agreement by name or use specific terminology, provided it clearly communicates acceptance of an agreement.

Whether announcements from the listed countries represent a ceasefire agreement will be primarily determined through the announcements themselves. Where a potentially qualifying announcement is made by all listed countries but, based on the announcements, it remains ambiguous whether the announcements represent a ceasefire agreement between the countries, this market will remain open until either i) definitive confirmation that the announcements represent a qualifying diplomatic agreement between the listed entities is achieved through further announcements from the listed countries/parties or a consensus of credible reporting or ii) 7 calendar days (ET) have passed after the date that the last country made their first potentially qualifying announcement. If, at the end of the seventh calendar day, no definitive confirmation has been achieved, the announcements will be judged based on the totality of information available from the resolution sources at that time. No single statement, denial, or presentation of evidence will govern where it is contradicted by the totality of information.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from the government of Saudi Arabia and Houthi leadership; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

market.question: Israeli airspace closed by October 31, 2026?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Israeli Airspace (The Tel Aviv Flight Information Region (FIR)/LLLL) is closed between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A qualifying closure occurs when the aviation or governmental authority responsible for overseeing the specified airspace region issues a Notice to Airmen (NOTAM), or other official order under the regulations of the jurisdiction responsible for that airspace region, which generally cancels or suspends commercial aviation across the specified airspace region, and such closure is not excluded under the exclusions provision below. A qualifying closure must apply generally to commercial flights transiting, arriving in, and departing from the specified airspace region. A closure is not disqualified because the order permits limited exceptions, including humanitarian, medical, repatriation, or emergency flights, or select flights authorized by the responsible authority, provided that commercial flights are prohibited by default, rather than permitted subject to conditions or restrictions.

The following are not qualifying closures: (i) closures due to weather, including volcanic and seismic activity; (ii) closures for holidays or religious observances; (iii) closures planned or announced before Contract Issuance; (iv) closures occurring on a regular cadence whose occurrence was determined before Contract Issuance, even if not announced; (v) closures resulting from the failure or malfunction of air traffic control, navigation, communications, power, or other technical systems; (vi) restrictions applying to aircraft by nationality, state of registry, operator, or ownership rather than to commercial traffic generally; (vii) closures of a subset of the specified airspace region, including geographic sectors and altitude bands; (viii) ground stops, flow restrictions, capacity reductions, or other air traffic management measures that delay or restrict traffic without closing the specified airspace region to commercial aviation; and (ix) warnings, no-fly zones, flight suspensions, or other restrictions imposed by any party other than the aviation or governmental authorities responsible for overseeing the specified airspace region.

A qualifying closure is deemed to occur at the time the closure takes effect, regardless of when the closure is announced or the order is issued. Where no effective time is included in the order, the closure is deemed to take effect at the time the order is issued.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from the Israeli government, including the Ministry of Transport, the Civil Aviation Authority, and the Israel Airports Authority, and a consensus of credible reporting.
